title.zh: 卷三百〇五 列傳第六十四 楊億 晁迥 劉筠 薛映
title.en: Volume 305 Biographies 64: Yang Yi, Chao Jiong, Liu Yun, Xue Ying
title.raw: 卷三百〇五 列傳第六十四 楊億 晁迥 劉筠 薛映 Volume 305 Biographies 64: Yang Yi, Chao Jiong, Liu Yun, Xue Ying

sentences.zh: 楊億，字大年，建州浦城人。

translations.literal: Yang Yi, style name Danian, was a man of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi, styled Danian, was a native of Pucheng in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖文逸，南唐玉山令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wen Yi was magistrate of Yushan under Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wen Yi had served as magistrate of Yushan under the Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 億將生，文逸夢一道士，自稱懷玉山人來謁，未幾，億生，有毛被體，長尺餘，經月乃落。

translations.literal: When Yi was about to be born, Wen Yi dreamed of a Daoist who called himself the Hermit of Huaiyu coming to pay a visit. Before long Yi was born, his body covered in hair more than a foot long, which fell away only after a month.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly before Yi was born, Wen Yi dreamed that a Daoist identifying himself as the Hermit of Huaiyu came to call on him. Soon afterward Yi was born with hair covering his entire body, more than a foot in length; it did not fall away until a month had passed.

sentences.zh: 能言，母以小經口授，隨即成誦。

translations.literal: He could speak; his mother orally taught him the Lesser Classics, and he could recite them at once.
translations.idiomatic: He learned to speak early. His mother taught him the Lesser Classics by recitation, and he could repeat them back immediately.

sentences.zh: 七歲，能屬文，對客談論，有老成風。

translations.literal: At seven he could compose prose; when conversing with guests he had the bearing of an old hand.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven he could compose literary pieces, and when he conversed with guests he carried himself with the poise of a seasoned man.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，年十一，太宗聞其名，詔江南轉運使張去華就試詞藝，送闕下。

translations.literal: In the early Yongxi era, at eleven, Taizong heard his name and ordered the Jiangnan transport commissioner Zhang Quhua to test his literary arts on the spot and send him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongxi reign, when he was eleven, Emperor Taizong heard of him and ordered Zhang Quhua, the Jiangnan transport commissioner, to examine his literary skill locally and then send him to court.

sentences.zh: 連三日得對，試詩賦五篇，下筆立成。

translations.literal: For three days in succession he was granted audience; he was tested with five poems and fu compositions and finished them as soon as he put brush to paper.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted audience three days running and asked to produce five poems and rhapsodies, each of which he completed the moment he set brush to paper.

sentences.zh: 太宗深加賞異，命內侍都知王仁睿送至中書，又賦詩一章，宰相驚其俊異，削章為賀。

translations.literal: Taizong was deeply impressed and had the chief eunuch Wang Renrui escort him to the Secretariat; he also composed a poem. The chief ministers marveled at his brilliance and trimmed their memorials into congratulatory notes.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was deeply impressed and had the chief eunuch Wang Renrui escort him to the Secretariat, while the emperor himself composed a poem in his honor. The chief ministers were astonished at the boy's brilliance and reshaped their memorials into letters of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 翌日，下制曰：「汝方髫齔，不由師訓，精爽神助，文字生知。

translations.literal: The next day an edict was issued saying: "You are still in childhood, yet without teachers' instruction your spirit is keen and divinely aided, and writing comes to you by innate knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict was issued: "Though you are still a child in your topknot, without formal instruction your spirit is keen—as if heaven aided you—and writing comes to you by innate gift.

sentences.zh: 越景絕塵，一日千里，予有望於汝也。

translations.literal: You surpass the scene and leave the dust behind; in a single day you cover a thousand li—I have high hopes for you.
translations.idiomatic: You outpace the horizon and leave the dust behind; in a single day you cover a thousand li. I have great expectations of you.

sentences.zh: 」即授秘書省正字，特賜袍笏。

translations.literal: " He was at once appointed Rectifier of Texts in the Secretariat and specially granted robe and court tablet.
translations.idiomatic: " He was immediately appointed Rectifier of Texts in the Secretariat and was specially granted an official robe and court tablet.

sentences.zh: 俄丁外艱，服除，會從祖徽之知許州，億往依焉。

translations.literal: Soon after he mourned his father; when mourning ended, it happened that his grand-uncle Huizhi was prefect of Xuzhou, and Yi went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered mourning for his father. When the mourning period ended, his grand-uncle Huizhi happened to be serving as prefect of Xuzhou, and Yi went to live under his care.

sentences.zh: 務學，晝夜不息，徽之間與語，歎曰：「興吾門者在汝矣。」

translations.literal: He devoted himself to study day and night without rest. When Huizhi conversed with him in private he sighed and said: "The one who will raise up our house is you."
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself to study without cease, day and night. When Huizhi spoke with him in private he sighed and said, "The one who will revive our clan is you."

sentences.zh: 淳化中，詣闕獻文，改太常寺奉禮郎，仍令讀書秘閣。

translations.literal: During the Chunhua era he went to court to present writings, was changed to Ceremonial Attendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was still ordered to study in the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua reign he went to court to present his writings, was promoted to Ceremonial Attendant in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was permitted to continue his studies in the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 獻《二京賦》，命試翰林，賜進士第，遷光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: He presented the "Rhapsody on the Two Capitals," was ordered tested by the Hanlin Academy, was granted the jinshi degree, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He presented his "Rhapsody on the Two Capitals," was examined by the Hanlin Academy, was granted the jinshi degree, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 屬後苑賞花曲宴，太宗召命賦詩於坐側；

translations.literal: When there was a flower-viewing banquet with music in the rear garden, Taizong summoned him and ordered him to compose a poem at his side;
translations.idiomatic: On the occasion of a musical flower-viewing banquet in the rear garden, Taizong summoned him and ordered him to compose a poem at the emperor's side;

sentences.zh: 又上《金明池頌》，太宗誦其警句於宰相。

translations.literal: he also submitted the "Ode to the Jinming Pond," and Taizong recited its striking lines to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: he also submitted an "Ode to the Jinming Pond," and Taizong recited its most striking lines to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，苑中曲宴，億復以詩獻。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, at another garden banquet with music, Yi again presented a poem.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year, at another musical banquet in the imperial garden, Yi again presented a poem.

sentences.zh: 太宗訝有司不時召，宰相言：「舊制，未貼職者不預。

translations.literal: Taizong wondered why the authorities had not summoned him in time; the chief ministers said: "By old regulation, those without a posted office do not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was surprised that the authorities had not summoned him in time. The chief ministers explained, "Under the old regulations, those without a posted appointment do not take part.

sentences.zh: 」即以億直集賢院。

translations.literal: " Yi was at once made a duty officer of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi was immediately assigned as a duty officer in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 表求歸鄉里，賜錢十五萬。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting to return to his home district and was granted one hundred fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial asking to return to his home district and was granted one hundred fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 至道初，太宗親製九弦琴、五弦阮，文士奏頌者眾，獨稱億為優，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhidao era Taizong personally made a nine-string qin and a five-string ruan; many literati submitted eulogies, but only Yi was praised as superior, and he was granted crimson fish insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhidao reign Taizong personally crafted a nine-string zither and a five-string ruan. Many scholars submitted eulogies, but Yi alone was singled out as the finest and was granted crimson fish insignia.

sentences.zh: 二年春，遷著作佐郎，帝知其貧，屢有沾賚，嘗命為越王生辰使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he was promoted to Assistant Compiler; the emperor knew he was poor and repeatedly bestowed gifts, and once appointed him birthday envoy to the Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he was promoted to Assistant Compiler. Knowing that he was poor, the emperor repeatedly bestowed gifts upon him and once appointed him birthday envoy to the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 時公卿表疏，多假文於億，名稱益著。

translations.literal: At the time many memorials of high officials borrowed his writing, and his reputation grew ever more prominent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many memorials from high officials were drafted with Yi's help, and his reputation grew ever more prominent.

sentences.zh: 真宗在京府，徽之為首僚，邸中書疏，悉億草定。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong was in the capital residence, Huizhi was chief staff officer; all documents in the residence were drafted by Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong was still heir apparent in the Eastern Palace, Huizhi served as his chief staff officer, and Yi drafted all the official documents for the residence.

sentences.zh: 即位初，超拜左正言。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his accession Yi was promoted out of turn to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after Zhenzong's accession, Yi was promoted out of turn to Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 詔錢若水修《太宗實錄》，奏億參預，凡八十卷，而億獨草五十六卷。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qian Ruoshui to compile the Veritable Records of Taizong; he memorialized that Yi should participate. The work totaled eighty juan, of which Yi alone drafted fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Qian Ruoshui to compile the Veritable Records of Taizong. He recommended Yi for the project; the work ran to eighty juan in all, of which Yi alone drafted fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 書成，乞外補就養，知處州。

translations.literal: When the book was finished he begged an outside appointment to support his parents and was made prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was finished he requested an outside post so that he could care for his parents and was appointed prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 真宗稱其才長於史學，留不遣，固請，乃許之任。

translations.literal: Zhenzong said his talent lay especially in historical studies and kept him from going; he pressed his request firmly, and only then was he allowed to take the post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong praised his talent for historical scholarship and refused to let him leave. Yi pressed his request repeatedly, and only then was he permitted to take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 郡人周啟明篤學有文，深加禮待。

translations.literal: A man of the prefecture, Zhou Qiming, was devoted to learning and possessed literary talent; Yi treated him with deep courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: A local scholar named Zhou Qiming was devoted to learning and gifted in letters; Yi treated him with exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 召還，拜左司諫、知制誥，賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was recalled, appointed Left Censorate Remonstrator and Drafting Drafter, and granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court, appointed Left Censorate Remonstrator and Drafting Drafter for Imperial Edicts, and granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，西鄙未寧，詔近臣議靈州棄守之事。

translations.literal: During the Xianping era the western frontier was not settled; the court ordered close ministers to discuss abandoning the defense of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping reign, with the western frontier still unsettled, the court ordered senior officials to debate whether Lingzhou should be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 億上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 「臣嘗讀史，見漢武北築朔方之郡，平津侯諫，以為罷敝中國，以奉無用之地，願罷之。

translations.literal: "Your servant has read history and seen that when Emperor Wu of Han built the Shuo-fang commandery in the north, the Marquis of Pingjin remonstrated, holding that it would exhaust China to supply a useless region and asking that it be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant has read in history that when Emperor Wu of Han established the Shuo-fang commandery in the north, the Marquis of Pingjin remonstrated, arguing that it would exhaust the empire to sustain a useless region and asking that the project be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 上使辯士朱買臣等發十策以難平津，平津不能對。

translations.literal: The emperor had debaters such as Zhu Maichen raise ten objections to refute Pingjin, and Pingjin could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had debaters such as Zhu Maichen raise ten objections to refute the marquis, and Pingjin could not answer them.

sentences.zh: 臣以為平津為賢相，非不能折買臣之舌，蓋所以將順人君之意爾。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that Pingjin was a worthy minister and was not unable to silence Maichen's tongue; he simply wished to follow and accommodate the ruler's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes that Pingjin was a worthy minister and was not incapable of silencing Zhu Maichen; he simply chose to follow and accommodate his sovereign's wishes.

sentences.zh: 舊稱朔方，地在要荒之外，聲教不及。

translations.literal: Formerly called Shuo-fang, the region lay beyond the vital wastes, where royal instruction did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: The region once known as Shuo-fang lay beyond the outer marches, where the court's civilizing influence did not reach.

sentences.zh: 元朔中，大將軍衛青奮兵掠地，列置郡縣。

translations.literal: In the Yuanshuo era the Grand General Wei Qing exerted troops to seize territory and established commanderies and counties in array.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanshuo reign, Grand General Wei Qing led his armies in conquest and established a network of commanderies and counties there.

sentences.zh: 今靈州蓋朔方之故墟，僻介西鄙，數百里間無有水草，烽火亭障不相望。

translations.literal: Present Lingzhou is roughly the old site of Shuo-fang, remote on the western border; for several hundred li there is no water or grass, and beacon towers and frontier posts do not look upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: Present-day Lingzhou occupies what was once the territory of Shuo-fang. Remote on the western frontier, for hundreds of li there is neither water nor pasture, and beacon towers and frontier posts stand too far apart to see one another.

sentences.zh: 當其道路不壅，饢饋無虞，猶足以張大國之威聲，為中原之扞蔽。

translations.literal: When its roads were not blocked and grain transport was secure, it could still suffice to display the great state's prestige and serve as a bulwark for the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: When its roads were open and supplies could be transported without fear, it could still magnify the prestige of the empire and serve as a shield for the central plains.

sentences.zh: 自邊境屢驚，凶黨猖熾，爵賞之而不恭，討罰之而無獲。

translations.literal: Since the border has been repeatedly alarmed, the hostile factions have grown rampant; enfeoffment and rewards do not win their respect, and punitive campaigns gain nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Since the frontier has been repeatedly disturbed, hostile factions have grown ever bolder: honors and rewards fail to win their submission, and punitive campaigns gain nothing.

sentences.zh: 自曹光實、白守榮、馬紹忠及王榮之敗，資糧屝屨，所失至多，將士丁夫，相枕而死。

translations.literal: Since the defeats of Cao Guangshi, Bai Shourong, Ma Shaozhong, and Wang Rong, provisions and footwear have been lost in great quantity, and soldiers and laborers have died lying one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Since the defeats suffered by Cao Guangshi, Bai Shourong, Ma Shaozhong, and Wang Rong, supplies and equipment have been lost in vast quantities, and soldiers and laborers have died in heaps upon one another.

sentences.zh: 以至募商人輸帛入穀，償價數倍；

translations.literal: It has reached the point of recruiting merchants to transport silk in exchange for grain, with compensation several times the value;
translations.idiomatic: Matters have reached the point where merchants must be recruited to deliver silk in exchange for grain, with compensation several times the goods' value;

sentences.zh: 孤壤築城，邊民繹騷，國帑匱乏，不能制邊人之命，及濟靈武之急。

translations.literal: cities are built on barren soil, frontier people are in constant uproar, the national treasury is depleted, and the court cannot control the border people's lives or relieve Lingwu's urgency.
translations.idiomatic: fortresses are built on barren ground, frontier populations are in constant turmoil, the national treasury is exhausted, and the court can neither command the border peoples nor relieve the crisis at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，凶黨逾盛。

translations.literal: Within a few years the hostile factions have grown ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the hostile factions have grown stronger still.

sentences.zh: 靈武危堞，巋然僅存，河外五城，繼聞陷沒。

translations.literal: Lingwu's perilous ramparts stand alone barely surviving; the five cities beyond the river have been heard to fall one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwu's battered walls stand barely intact, while five cities beyond the river have fallen in succession.

sentences.zh: 但堅壁清野，坐食糗糧，閉壘枕戈，苟度朝夕，未粕出一兵，馳一騎，敢與之角。

translations.literal: They only strengthen walls and clear the countryside, sit eating dry provisions, close the forts and sleep on their weapons, barely passing day and night, never yet sending out a soldier or dispatching a rider to dare contest with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison merely strengthens its walls, clears the countryside, consumes its stores, bars the gates, and sleeps beside its weapons, barely surviving from day to day—never yet sending out a single soldier or rider to contest the enemy.

sentences.zh: 此靈武之存無益，明矣。

translations.literal: That Lingwu's survival is of no benefit is clear.
translations.idiomatic: It is plain that holding Lingwu serves no purpose.

sentences.zh: 平津所言罷敝中國以奉無用之地，正今日謂也。

translations.literal: What Pingjin said about exhausting China to supply a useless region is precisely what applies today.
translations.idiomatic: What the Marquis of Pingjin said about exhausting the empire to sustain a useless region applies exactly to the present situation.

sentences.zh: 臣以為存有大害，棄有大利，國家免粟之勞，士卒流離之苦，悉皆免焉。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that keeping it has great harm and abandoning it has great benefit: the state would be freed from the labor of grain transport and soldiers from the suffering of displacement—all would be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes that retaining it brings great harm while abandoning it brings great benefit: the state would be spared the labor of grain transport and the troops the suffering of exile—all of this would be eliminated at once.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜、禹，聖之盛者也，地不過數千里，而明德格天，四門穆穆。

translations.literal: Yao, Shun, and Yu were the greatest of sages; their domains did not exceed several thousand li, yet their bright virtue reached heaven and the Four Gates were serene.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, Shun, and Yu were the greatest of sages. Their domains extended no more than several thousand li, yet their luminous virtue reached heaven and peace reigned at the Four Gates.

sentences.zh: 武丁、成王，商、周之明主也，然地東不過江、黃，西不過氐、羌，南不過蠻荊，北不過太原，而頌聲並作，號為至治。

translations.literal: King Wuding and King Cheng were enlightened rulers of Shang and Zhou; yet their lands east did not pass the Yangtze and Yellow rivers, west did not pass the Di and Qiang, south did not pass the southern barbarians and Jing, north did not pass Taiyuan—and yet songs of praise arose together and they were called reaching the utmost governance.
translations.idiomatic: King Wuding of Shang and King Cheng of Zhou were enlightened sovereigns, yet their domains extended no farther east than the Yangtze and Yellow rivers, no farther west than the Di and Qiang peoples, no farther south than the southern barbarians and Jing region, and no farther north than Taiyuan—yet songs of praise arose everywhere and their reigns were hailed as the height of good government.

sentences.zh: 及秦、漢窮兵拓土，肝腦塗地，校其功德，豈可同年而語哉！

translations.literal: When Qin and Han exhausted troops to expand territory and brains and blood smeared the ground, comparing their merit and virtue—how can they be spoken of in the same year!
translations.idiomatic: When Qin and Han exhausted their armies in territorial expansion until brains and blood stained the ground, how can their achievements be mentioned in the same breath as those of the sage kings!

sentences.zh: 昔西漢賈捐之建議棄朱崖，當時公卿，亦有異論，元帝力排眾說，奮乎獨見，下詔廢之，人頌其德。

translations.literal: Formerly in Western Han Jia Juanzhi proposed abandoning Zhuya; at the time the high officials also had differing views, but Emperor Yuan forcefully rejected the crowd's opinions, boldly holding a lone view, issued an edict to abolish it, and people praised his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In Western Han, Jia Juanzhi proposed abandoning Zhuya. Many high officials disagreed, but Emperor Yuan forcefully rejected the majority view, acted on his own conviction, issued an edict abolishing the commandery, and the people praised his wisdom.

sentences.zh: 故其詔曰：「議者以棄朱崖羞威不行，夫通於時變，即憂萬民之饑鋨，危孰大焉。

translations.literal: Therefore his edict said: "Those who discuss the matter hold that abandoning Zhuya shames us because prestige will not be enforced—but one who understands changing times immediately worries over the people's famine distress; what peril is greater?
translations.idiomatic: His edict declared: "Critics say that abandoning Zhuya would shame us because our prestige would go unenforced—but one who understands the needs of the times must first worry over the people's hunger and distress. What peril could be greater?

sentences.zh: 且宗廟之祭，凶年不備，況乎避不嫌之辱哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, sacrifices at the ancestral temple are not complete in famine years—how much less should one avoid the disgrace of an unseemly slight!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when famine years come the ancestral sacrifices cannot even be properly performed—how much less should one cling to the shame of a slight loss of face!"

sentences.zh: 」臣以為類於靈武也，必以失地為言，即燕、薊八州，河湟五郡，所失多矣，何必此為？

translations.literal: " Your servant considers this analogous to Lingwu. If one must speak of lost territory, the eight prefectures of Yan and Ji and the five commanderies of Hehuang have been lost in far greater measure—why fix on this alone?
translations.idiomatic: " Your servant believes the case is analogous to Lingwu. If the argument is that we must not lose territory, consider that the eight prefectures of Yan and Ji and the five commanderies of the Hehuang region have already been lost in far greater measure—why fix on this one place alone?

sentences.zh: 臣竊惟太祖命姚內斌領慶州，董遵誨領環州，統兵才五六千，悉付以閫外之事，士卒效命，疆埸晏然，朝廷無旰食之憂，疆埸無羽書之警。

translations.literal: Your servant privately reflects that Taizu appointed Yao Neibin to command Qingzhou and Dong Zunhui to command Huanzhou, each with only five or six thousand troops, yet entrusted them entirely with matters beyond the pass; soldiers gave their lives, the frontier was tranquil, the court had no worry of eating late, and the frontier had no alarm of urgent dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant recalls that Taizu appointed Yao Neibin to command Qingzhou and Dong Zunhui to command Huanzhou with only five or six thousand troops each, yet entrusted them with full authority beyond the passes. Their soldiers served devotedly, the frontier remained tranquil, the court had no need to dine late in anxiety, and no urgent dispatches arrived from the border.

sentences.zh: 臣乞選將臨邊，賜給廩賦，資以策略，許以便宜而行。

translations.literal: Your servant begs to select generals to oversee the border, grant them grain rations and tax revenues, supply them with strategy, and permit them to act as circumstances require.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks that able generals be chosen to command the frontier, granted grain rations and local revenues, supplied with strategy, and permitted to act on their own discretion as circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 儻寇擾內屬，撓之以勁兵，示之以大信，懷荒振遠，諭以賞格，彼則奔潰眾叛，安能與大邦為敵哉？

translations.literal: If the enemy harasses those who submit inward, harass them with strong troops, show them great good faith, cherish the distant and rouse the far, instruct them with reward standards—then they will flee in rout and the multitude will rebel; how could they match a great state as foes?
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy harasses tribes that have submitted, strike them with strong forces, show them the court's good faith, win over distant peoples, and offer clear rewards—then they will scatter in rout and their followers will desert them. How could they stand as enemies against a great power?

sentences.zh: 若欲謀成廟堂，功在漏刻，臣以為彼眾方黠，積財猶豐，未可以歲月破也。

translations.literal: If one wishes to complete the plan at court and achieve merit within a clepsydra's drip, your servant holds that their masses are now cunning and their accumulated wealth still abundant—they cannot be broken within months and years.
translations.idiomatic: If one hopes to complete the court's strategy and achieve success within a matter of hours, your servant believes the enemy is now cunning and their accumulated wealth still abundant—they cannot be broken within a few months or years.

sentences.zh: 直須棄靈州，保環慶，然後以計困之爾。

translations.literal: One must simply abandon Lingzhou, protect Huan and Qing, and then use stratagem to wear them down.
translations.idiomatic: One must simply abandon Lingzhou, secure Huanzhou and Qingzhou, and then use strategy to wear the enemy down.

sentences.zh: 如臣之策，得驍將數人，提銳兵一二萬，給數縣賦以資所用，令分守邊城，則寇可就擒，而朝廷得以無虞矣。」

translations.literal: According to your servant's plan, obtaining several fierce generals, leading ten or twenty thousand elite troops, granting several counties' revenues to supply their needs, and ordering them to divide and guard frontier cities—then the enemy can be captured and the court can be without worry."
translations.idiomatic: According to your servant's plan, if several able generals are obtained, ten or twenty thousand elite troops are led forth, revenues from several counties are granted for their expenses, and they are ordered to divide forces and guard the frontier cities, the enemy can be brought to bay and the court will be free of concern."

sentences.zh: 景德初，以家貧，乞典郡江左，詔令知通進銀司兼門下封駁事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingde era, because his family was poor he begged to administer a prefecture on the lower Yangtze; an edict ordered him to know the Office for Presenting Memorials and Tribute and concurrently handle seal-and-return matters at the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde reign, citing his family's poverty, he requested an appointment as prefect on the lower Yangtze. The court instead ordered him to direct the Office for Presenting Memorials and Tribute while concurrently handling seal-and-return review at the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 時以吏部銓主事前宜黃簿王太沖為大理評事，億以丞吏之賤，不宜任清秩，即封詔還。

translations.literal: At the time the Ministry of Personnel's chief clerk Wang Taichong, formerly keeper of the yellow registers, was appointed Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review; Yi held that a lowly clerk should not hold a pure rank and at once sealed the edict and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Taichong, a chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel who had formerly kept the yellow registers, was appointed Assessor in the Court of Judicial Review. Yi argued that a lowly clerical officer should not hold so exalted a post and immediately sealed the edict and returned it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，太沖補外。

translations.literal: Before long Taichong was given an outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang was reassigned to an outside post.

sentences.zh: 俄判史館，會修《冊府元龜》，億與王欽若同總其事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made concurrent director of the History Office; when the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives was compiled, Yi and Wang Qinruo jointly oversaw the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made concurrent director of the History Office. When the court undertook the compilation of the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives, Yi and Wang Qinruo jointly directed the project.

sentences.zh: 其序次體制，皆億所定，群僚分撰篇序，詔經億竄定方用之。

translations.literal: Its ordering, arrangement, and system were all set by Yi; the various officials drafted sections and prefaces by division, and an edict required passage through Yi's revision before use.
translations.idiomatic: The work's organization and editorial principles were all established by Yi. Other officials drafted individual sections and prefaces, but an edict required that everything pass through Yi's revision before it could be used.

sentences.zh: 三年，召為翰林學士，又同修國史，凡變例多出億手。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned as Hanlin Academician and also jointly compiled the National History; most changes in precedent came from Yi's hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was summoned as Hanlin Academician and also appointed to compile the National History jointly; most revisions to precedent came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，加兵部員外郎、戶部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong Xiangfu era he was given additional posts as Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu reign he was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 五年，以疾在告，遣中使致太醫視之，億拜章謝，上作詩批紙尾，有「副予前席待名賢」之句。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on sick leave, the court sent an inner envoy with the imperial physician to examine him; Yi submitted a memorial of thanks, and the emperor wrote a poem on the margin with the line "matching my forward seat awaiting famed worthies."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he took sick leave, and the court sent an imperial envoy with the court physician to examine him. Yi submitted a memorial of thanks, and the emperor wrote a poem on the margin that included the line, "worthy of the seat I keep ready for eminent men."

sentences.zh: 以久疾，求解近職，優詔不許，但權免朝直。

translations.literal: Because of long illness he requested relief from a nearby post; a gracious edict did not permit it but only temporarily excused him from dawn attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his prolonged illness he asked to be relieved of his court duties. A gracious edict refused the request but temporarily excused him from dawn attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 億剛介寡合，在書局，唯與李維、路振、刁衎、陳越、劉筠輩厚善。

translations.literal: Yi was upright and aloof, rarely in accord with others; in the book office he was thick friends only with Li Wei, Lu Zhen, Diao Yan, Chen Yue, Liu Yun, and their sort.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was upright and aloof and had few close associates. In the book office he was on especially close terms only with Li Wei, Lu Zhen, Diao Yan, Chen Yue, Liu Yun, and their circle.

sentences.zh: 當時文士，咸賴其題品，或被貶議者，退多怨誹。

translations.literal: Literati of the time all relied on his judgments of merit; those he criticized or demoted often harbored resentment and slander in private.
translations.idiomatic: Literati of the day all relied on his judgments of literary merit. Those he criticized or passed over often nursed resentment and spoke against him in private.

sentences.zh: 王欽若驟貴，億素薄其人，欽若銜之，屢抉其失；

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo rose swiftly in rank; Yi had always looked down on him, and Qinruo bore a grudge and repeatedly seized on his faults;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo rose swiftly in rank. Yi had long held him in low regard, and Wang bore a grudge, repeatedly seizing on Yi's faults;

sentences.zh: 陳彭年方以文史售進，忌億名出其右，相與毀訾。

translations.literal: Chen Pengnian was then advancing by selling his literary and historical skill; he resented that Yi's fame stood above his, and together they slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian was then advancing through his literary and historical accomplishments. Jealous that Yi's reputation outshone his own, he joined Wang in denigrating him.

sentences.zh: 上素重億，皆不惑其說。

translations.literal: The emperor had always valued Yi and was not swayed by any of their talk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always held Yi in high regard and was not swayed by their accusations.

sentences.zh: 億有別墅在陽翟，億母往視之，因得疾，請歸省，不待報而行。

translations.literal: Yi had a villa at Yangdi; his mother went to visit it and fell ill. He requested leave to return home to see her and departed without awaiting reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yi owned a villa at Yangdi. When his mother went there to visit and fell ill, he requested leave to return home and set out without waiting for a reply.

sentences.zh: 上親緘藥劑，加金帛以賜。

translations.literal: The emperor personally sealed medicine and added gold and silk as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally sealed medicines for her and added gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 億素體羸，至是，以病聞，請解官。

translations.literal: Yi had always been frail in body; by this time his illness was reported and he requested to resign his office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had always been frail. Now, with word of his illness reaching court, he requested to resign his post.

sentences.zh: 有嗾憲官劾億不俟命而去，授太常少卿，分司西京，許就所居養療。

translations.literal: Someone incited a censor to impeach Yi for leaving without awaiting orders; he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with duty at the Western Capital, permitted to convalesce at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Someone prompted a censor to impeach Yi for departing without awaiting permission. He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with duty at the Western Capital and was permitted to recuperate at his home.

sentences.zh: 嘗作《君可思賦》，以抒忠憤。

translations.literal: He once composed the "Rhapsody on Whether the Ruler May Be Pondered" to express loyal indignation.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed the "Rhapsody on Whether the Ruler May Be Pondered" to give voice to his loyal indignation.

sentences.zh: 《冊府元龜》成，進秩秘書監。

translations.literal: When the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives was completed he was advanced in rank to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives was completed, he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 七年，病愈，起知汝州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when his illness healed, he was raised to administer Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after he recovered, he was reappointed prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 會加上玉皇聖號，表求陪預，即代還，以為參詳儀制副使，知禮儀院，判秘閣、太常寺。

translations.literal: When the Sagely Title of the Jade Emperor was added, he memorialized requesting to participate; he was at once replaced and recalled, made Deputy Commissioner for Reviewing Ritual Regulations, director of the Court of Ritual, and concurrent director of the Imperial Library and Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the court added the Sagely Title of the Jade Emperor, he memorialized asking to take part in the ceremonies. He was immediately recalled and appointed Deputy Commissioner for Reviewing Ritual Regulations, director of the Court of Ritual, and concurrent director of the Imperial Library and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年冬，拜工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Tianxi he was appointed Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Tianxi he was appointed Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明年，權同知貢舉，坐考較差謬，降授秘書監。

translations.literal: The next year he was acting Associate Commissioner for the Examination; because of errors in grading he was demoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served as acting Associate Commissioner for the civil service examinations. Because of errors in grading he was demoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，屬行郊禮，以億典司禮樂，未卒哭，起復工部侍郎，令視事。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when the suburban sacrifice was to be performed, because Yi directed ritual and music he was raised before mourning ended to Vice Minister of Works and ordered to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother. Because a suburban sacrifice was scheduled and Yi was responsible for ritual and music, he was recalled to service before the mourning period had ended, restored as Vice Minister of Works, and ordered to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 四年，復為翰林學士，受詔注釋御集，又兼史館修撰、判館事，權景靈宮副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was again Hanlin Academician, received an edict to annotate the imperial collected writings, and was also concurrent History Office compiler, director of the office, and acting deputy commissioner of the Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was again appointed Hanlin Academician and received an edict to annotate the emperor's collected writings. He also served concurrently as compiler in the History Office and director of that office, with acting duty as deputy commissioner of the Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月，卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he died at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 錄其子紘為太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: His son Hong was entered on the register as Ceremonial Attendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong was entered on the register as Ceremonial Attendant in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 億天性穎悟，自幼及終，不離翰墨。

translations.literal: Yi was keen and perceptive by nature; from youth to the end he never left brush and ink.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was keen-witted by nature and from childhood to the end of his life never set aside brush and ink.

sentences.zh: 文格雄健，才思敏捷，略不凝滯，對客談笑，揮翰不輟。

translations.literal: His literary style was bold and strong, his talent swift, scarcely ever hesitating; while conversing and laughing with guests he wielded the brush without pause.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was vigorous, his wit swift, and he scarcely ever hesitated over a word. Even while conversing and laughing with guests he wrote without pause.

sentences.zh: 精密有規裁，善細字起草，一幅數千言，不加點竄，當時學者，翕然宗之。

translations.literal: He was precise and had rules of judgment, skilled at drafting in fine characters; a single sheet of several thousand words needed no correction, and scholars of the time all revered him together.
translations.idiomatic: He was meticulous and exacting in judgment, skilled at drafting in fine hand: a single sheet of several thousand characters required no revision, and scholars of the day revered him as a master.

sentences.zh: 而博覽強記，尤長典章制度，時多取正。

translations.literal: Moreover he read widely and remembered strongly, especially excelling in statutes and institutions; the age often sought his correction.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and remembered with exceptional strength, especially in statutes and institutional precedent, which many of his contemporaries consulted him to settle.

sentences.zh: 喜誨誘後進，以成名者甚眾。

translations.literal: He delighted in instructing and guiding the younger generation; very many achieved fame through him.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in guiding younger scholars, and a great many who achieved renown did so under his tutelage.

sentences.zh: 人有片辭可紀，必為諷誦。

translations.literal: If someone had even a fragment worth recording, he would certainly recite it in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever someone produced even a line worth remembering, he would recite it aloud in appreciation.

sentences.zh: 手集當世之述作，為《筆苑時文錄》數十篇。

translations.literal: He personally collected contemporary writings into several tens of sections of the Records of Brush-Garden Timely Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He personally collected contemporary writings into several dozen sections of the Records of Brush-Garden Timely Literature.

sentences.zh: 重交遊，性耿介，尚名節。

translations.literal: He valued friendship, was upright and aloof by nature, and esteemed reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He valued friendship, was upright and unyielding by nature, and held reputation and integrity in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 多周給親友，故廩祿亦隨而盡。

translations.literal: He often aided relatives and friends, and therefore his salary and emoluments were also exhausted along with it.
translations.idiomatic: He gave generously to relatives and friends, and so his official salary was always spent as fast as it came.

sentences.zh: 留心釋典禪觀之學，所著《括蒼》、《武夷》、《潁陰》、《韓城》、《退居》、《汝陽》、《蓬山》、《冠鼇》等集、《內外制》、《刀筆》，共一百九十四卷。

translations.literal: He devoted attention to Buddhist scriptures and Chan contemplation; his works included the collected writings Kuocang, Wuyi, Yingyin, Hancheng, Tuiju, Ruyang, Pengshan, and Guan'ao, Inner and Outer Drafts, and Brush Notes—one hundred ninety-four juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to Buddhist scriptures and Chan meditation. His collected works included the Kuocang, Wuyi, Yingyin, Hancheng, Tuiju, Ruyang, Pengshan, and Guan'ao anthologies, along with Inner and Outer Drafts and Brush Notes—one hundred ninety-four juan in all.

sentences.zh: 弟倚，景德中舉進士，得第三等及第；

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi, in the Jingde era passed the jinshi examination and received third-rank passing;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yi passed the jinshi examination during the Jingde reign and was placed in the third rank;

sentences.zh: 以億故，升為第二等。

translations.literal: because of Yi he was raised to second rank.
translations.idiomatic: because of Yi's standing he was promoted to the second rank.

sentences.zh: 億無子，以從子紘為後。

translations.literal: Yi had no son and took his nephew Hong as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had no sons and adopted his nephew Hong as his heir.

sentences.zh: 弟偉。

translations.literal: Younger brother Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wei.

sentences.zh: 弟 偉

translations.literal: Younger brother Wei
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Wei

sentences.zh: 偉，字子奇，幼學於億。

translations.literal: Wei, style name Ziqi, studied in youth under Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, styled Ziqi, studied in his youth under his brother Yi.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年獻頌，召試學士院，賜進士及第。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi he presented a eulogy, was summoned for examination at the Academy, and was granted jinshi with passing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi he presented a eulogy, was summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy, and was granted the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 以試秘書省校書郎知衢州龍遊縣，再補蘄州錄事參軍，國子監薦為直講。

translations.literal: By examination he became Proofreader of the Secretariat and prefect of Longyou in Quzhou; he was again appointed Recorder of Qizhou and recommended by the Directorate of Education as Erudite Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the examination he was appointed Proofreader of the Secretariat and magistrate of Longyou County in Quzhou. He later served as Recorder in Qizhou and was recommended by the Directorate of Education as Erudite Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉李遵勖守澶州，辟簽書鎮寧軍節度判官事。

translations.literal: When the Commandant-in-Chief of the Imperial Son-in-Law Li Zunxu guarded Danzhou, he recruited Wei as drafting secretary for the military governor of Zhenning.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zunxu, Commandant-in-Chief of the Imperial Son-in-Law, was stationed at Danzhou, he recruited Wei as drafting secretary on the staff of the Zhenning military governor.

sentences.zh: 遷大理寺丞、知河間縣，再遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and prefect of Hejian, then again promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and appointed magistrate of Hejian County, then promoted again to Erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 用近臣薦，為集賢校理、通判單州。

translations.literal: On recommendation of a close minister he became Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and administrative vice-prefect of Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of a close court official he was appointed Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and administrative vice-prefect of Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 會巡檢部卒李素合州卒二百餘人，謀殺巡檢使，入鼓角門，州將不敢出。

translations.literal: It happened that patrol inspector troops under Li Su joined with more than two hundred prefectural troops to plot killing the patrol inspector, entered the drum-and-horn gate, and the prefectural commander dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: When patrol inspector Li Su joined with more than two hundred prefectural troops in a plot to kill the patrol inspector, they forced their way through the drum-and-horn gate. The prefectural commander dared not emerge.

sentences.zh: 偉挺身往問曰：「若屬何為而反？

translations.literal: Wei stepped forward and went to ask: "What are you doing in rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Wei stepped forward and demanded, "What are you rebelling for?

sentences.zh: 」俱曰：「將有訴於州，非反也。

translations.literal: " They all said: "We intend to lodge a complaint at the prefecture—it is not rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " They all replied, "We mean to lodge a complaint with the prefecture—we are not rebelling.

sentences.zh: 」偉曰：「持兵來，非反而何？

translations.literal: " Wei said: "Coming armed—if not rebellion, what is it?
translations.idiomatic: " Wei said, "You come bearing arms—if this is not rebellion, what is it?

sentences.zh: 若屬皆有父母妻子，以一朝忿而欲魚肉之乎？

translations.literal: You all have fathers, mothers, wives, and children—do you wish to make them meat and fish in a single morning's anger?
translations.idiomatic: You all have parents, wives, and children—would you slaughter them all in a single fit of anger?

sentences.zh: 」悉令投兵，坐籍首惡得十餘人，斬之。

translations.literal: " He ordered all to cast down weapons, sat in judgment and registered the chief culprits—more than ten—and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered them all to lay down their weapons, identified more than a dozen ringleaders, and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 徙知祥符縣、提點開封府界諸縣鎮公事，權開封府判官，又判三司開拆司，累遷尚書兵部員外郎、同修起居注。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Xiangfu County, became Commissioner for the counties and towns of the Kaifeng prefectural boundary, acting Kaifeng vice-prefect, and also judged the Three Departments' unpacking office; he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War in the Secretariat and joint compiler of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Xiangfu County, then appointed Commissioner for the counties and towns within the Kaifeng metropolitan boundary, acting vice-prefect of Kaifeng, and judge of the Three Departments' unpacking office. He rose through successive promotions to Vice Director of the Ministry of War and joint compiler of the Imperial Diary.

sentences.zh: 偉清慎，無治劇才，常秉小笏以朝，知制誥缺，中書以偉名進，仁宗曰：「此非秉小笏者邪？

translations.literal: Wei was pure and cautious, without talent for governing urgent affairs; he always held a small tablet at court. When the drafting drafter post was vacant the Secretariat advanced Wei's name; Renzong said: "Is this not the one who holds the small tablet?
translations.idiomatic: Wei was upright and cautious but lacked talent for handling urgent affairs. He always carried a small court tablet at audience. When the post of Drafting Drafter fell vacant the Secretariat recommended Wei. Renzong said, "Is this not the man who carries the small tablet?

sentences.zh: 」遂命知制誥。

translations.literal: " He then ordered him made Drafting Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: " Nevertheless he appointed him Drafting Drafter.

sentences.zh: 權諫院，嘗曰：「諫臣宜陳列大事，細故何足論。

translations.literal: He acted in the Remonstrance Bureau and once said: "Remonstrating officials should set forth great affairs—what are petty matters worth discussing?
translations.idiomatic: While acting in the Remonstrance Bureau he once said, "Remonstrating officials ought to address great matters of state—what are petty details worth debating?

sentences.zh: 」然當時譏其亡補。

translations.literal: " Yet at the time people mocked that he accomplished nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet contemporaries mocked him for accomplishing nothing of substance.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部郎中，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Punishments and made Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Punishments and appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 祀明堂，遷右司郎中、判太常寺，為群牧使兼侍讀學士，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the Bright Hall sacrifice he was promoted to Director of the Right Bureau, judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, became Commissioner of Herds with concurrent Study-Companion Academician, and advanced to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall sacrifice he was promoted to Director of the Right Bureau and made concurrent director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then Commissioner of Herds with concurrent Study-Companion Academician, and finally advanced to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Vice Minister of Rites in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子 紘

translations.literal: Son Hong
translations.idiomatic: Son Hong

sentences.zh: 紘，字望之，以蔭歷官知鄞縣，鄞濱海，惡少販魚鹽者，群居洲島，或掠商人財物入海，吏不能禁，紘至，設方略，使識者質惡少船，及歸，始給還，且戒諭之，由是不敢為盜。

translations.literal: Hong, style name Wangzhi, by yin privilege served in office and became prefect of Yin; Yin bordered the sea, and ruffians who trafficked in fish and salt dwelled in groups on islets, sometimes seizing merchants' goods and going to sea—the clerks could not stop them. When Hong arrived he devised a plan: trusted men would take the ruffians' boats in pledge, and only when they returned were they given back, with admonition—thereafter they dared not become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, styled Wangzhi, entered office through yin privilege and was appointed magistrate of Yin County. Yin lay on the coast, where ruffians who trafficked in fish and salt gathered on offshore islets and sometimes robbed merchants before fleeing to sea—officials could not stop them. Hong devised a scheme: trusted men would hold the ruffians' boats as pledge and return them only when the owners came back, with a stern warning. After that they dared not turn to banditry.

sentences.zh: 以億文獻，賜進士出身。

translations.literal: Because of Yi's literary offerings he was granted jinshi origin.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Yi's literary works presented to the throne, he was granted jinshi standing.

sentences.zh: 通判越州，知筠州，提點江東刑獄，除轉運、按察使。

translations.literal: He was vice-prefect of Yuezhou, prefect of Yunzhou, Commissioner for Jiangdong judicial punishments, and appointed transport and investigation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-prefect of Yuezhou, prefect of Yunzhou, and Commissioner for judicial affairs in Jiangdong, then was appointed transport and investigation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 江東饑，紘開義倉振之，吏持不可，紘曰：「義倉，為民也，稍稽，人將殍矣。」

translations.literal: Jiangdong suffered famine; Hong opened the charity granary to relieve it. The clerks held it impossible; Hong said: "The charity granary exists for the people—delay a little and they will starve to death."
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Jiangdong, Hong opened the charity granary to provide relief. His subordinates objected, but Hong said, "The charity granary exists for the people—delay even briefly and they will starve."

sentences.zh: 紘御下急，常曰：「不法之人不可貸，去之，止不利一家爾，豈可使郡邑千萬家俱受害邪？

translations.literal: Hong was stern in commanding subordinates and often said: "Lawless men cannot be pardoned—remove them and only one household is harmed; how can one let thousands of households in a prefecture all suffer harm?
translations.idiomatic: Hong was severe with subordinates and often said, "Lawless men must not be spared. Remove one and only a single household suffers—how can an entire prefecture of millions be allowed to suffer together?

sentences.zh: 」聞者望風解去，或過期不敢之官。

translations.literal: " Those who heard fled at the wind's report, or past their term dared not take office.
translations.idiomatic: " Wrongdoers fled at the mere rumor of his approach, and some dared not take up their posts even after their terms had expired.

sentences.zh: 與王鼎、王綽號「江東三虎」。

translations.literal: With Wang Ding and Wang Chuo he was called the "Three Tigers of Jiangdong."
translations.idiomatic: Together with Wang Ding and Wang Chuo he was known as the "Three Tigers of Jiangdong."

sentences.zh: 坐降知衡州，徙越州。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to prefect of Hengzhou and transferred to Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a demotion he was appointed prefect of Hengzhou, then transferred to Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 為荊南轉運使，徙福建，不赴，知湖州，復為江東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was Jingnan transport commissioner, transferred to Fujian but did not go, became prefect of Huzhou, and again served as Jiangdong transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as transport commissioner in Jingnan, was transferred to Fujian but declined to go, was appointed prefect of Huzhou, and later returned as Jiangdong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 官至太常少卿，卒。

translations.literal: He reached Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and died in office.

sentences.zh: 紘性嚴，雖家居，兒女不敢妄言笑。

translations.literal: Hong's nature was stern; even at home his sons and daughters dared not speak or laugh rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was stern by nature. Even at home his children dared not speak or laugh without permission.

sentences.zh: 聚書數萬卷，手抄事實，名《窺豹篇》。

translations.literal: He collected tens of thousands of juan of books, hand-copied factual matters, and named it Glimpsing the Leopard.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed tens of thousands of juan of books, copied factual extracts by hand, and compiled them under the title Glimpsing the Leopard.

sentences.zh: 晁迥，字明遠，世為澶州清豐人，自其父佺，始徙家彭門。

translations.literal: Chao Jiong, style name Mingyuan, for generations was a man of Qingfeng in Danzhou; from his father Quan the family first moved to Pengmen.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Jiong, styled Mingyuan, came from a family long established at Qingfeng in Danzhou. His father Quan was the first to move the household to Pengmen.

sentences.zh: 迥舉進士，為大理評事，歷知岳州錄事參軍，改將作監丞，稍遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: Jiong passed the jinshi examination, became Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, successively served as Recorder of Yuezhou, was changed to Vice Director of the Directorate of Works, and was gradually promoted to Director of the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Assessor in the Court of Judicial Review. He served successively as Recorder in Yuezhou, was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Works, and was gradually promoted to Director of the Palace Bureau.

sentences.zh: 坐失入囚死罪，奪二官。

translations.literal: For the offense of wrongful entry causing a prisoner's death he was stripped of two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Because a prisoner died through his wrongful intervention he was stripped of two ranks.

sentences.zh: 復將作丞，監徐、婺二州稅，遷太常丞。

translations.literal: He was restored as Vice Director of Works, supervised taxes in Xu and Wu prefectures, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Vice Director of Works, supervised tax collection in Xu and Wu prefectures, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，用宰相呂端、參知政事李沆薦，擢右正言、直史館。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, on recommendation of Chief Minister Lü Duan and Vice Grand Councillor Li Hang he was promoted to Right Remonstrator and duty officer of the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded to the throne, on the recommendation of Chief Minister Lü Duan and Vice Grand Councillor Li Hang he was promoted to Right Remonstrator and duty officer of the History Office.

sentences.zh: 獻《咸平新書》五十篇，又獻《理樞》一篇。

translations.literal: He presented fifty sections of the New Book of the Xianping Era and also one section of Pivot of Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He presented fifty sections of the New Book of the Xianping Era and also a treatise entitled Pivot of Governance.

sentences.zh: 召試，除右司諫、知制誥，判尚書刑部。

translations.literal: Summoned for examination, he was appointed Right Censorate Remonstrator and Drafting Drafter and made concurrent judge of the Ministry of Punishments in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After being summoned for examination he was appointed Right Censorate Remonstrator and Drafting Drafter, with concurrent duty as judge of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 帝北征，雍王元份留守京師，加右諫議大夫，為判官，進翰林學士。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned north, Prince Yong Yuanfen remained to guard the capital; Jiong was given Right Remonstrating Grand Master, made staff judge, and advanced to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched north, Prince Yong Yuanfen was left to guard the capital. Jiong was promoted to Right Remonstrating Grand Master, appointed staff judge, and advanced to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知審官院，為明德、章穆二園陵禮儀使，同修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he directed the Bureau of Review, was ritual commissioner for the Mingde and Zhangmu imperial park tombs, and jointly compiled the National History.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he directed the Bureau of Review, served as ritual commissioner for the Mingde and Zhangmu imperial tombs, and was appointed joint compiler of the National History.

sentences.zh: 知大中祥符元年貢舉。

translations.literal: He directed the civil service examinations of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the civil service examinations in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，祀汾陰，同太常詳定儀注，累遷尚書工部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the Mount Tai feng and Fen-yin sacrifices he joined the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in detailing ritual regulations and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Works in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the Mount Tai feng and Fen-yin sacrifices he worked with the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to fix ritual regulations and rose through successive promotions to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，還，奏《北庭記》，加史館修撰、知通進銀臺司。

translations.literal: As envoy to the Khitan, on return he submitted the Record of the Northern Court, was given additional post as History Office compiler, and directed the Office for Presenting Memorials and the Silver Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Sent as envoy to the Khitan, he submitted the Record of the Northern Court on his return and was additionally appointed History Office compiler and director of the Office for Presenting Memorials and the Silver Terrace.

sentences.zh: 獻《玉清昭應宮頌》，其子宗操繼上《景靈宮慶成歌》。

translations.literal: He presented the "Ode to the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace"; his son Zongcao followed with the "Song of Completion for the Jingling Palace."
translations.idiomatic: He presented an "Ode to the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace," and his son Zongcao followed with a "Song of Completion for the Jingling Palace."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「迥父子同獻歌頌，搢紳間美事也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Father and son Jiong together presenting songs of praise—among the gentry this is a fine matter."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked, "Father and son presenting songs of praise together—among the gentry this is a fine thing indeed."

sentences.zh: 史成，擢刑部侍郎，進承旨。

translations.literal: When the history was completed he was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments and advanced to Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: When the history was completed he was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments and advanced to Academician Expositor.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷方修禮文之事，詔令多出迥手。

translations.literal: At the time the court was just then repairing ritual and literary matters; edicts mostly came from Jiong's hand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was revising ritual and literary regulations, and most edicts issued from Jiong's hand.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜召對，帝令內侍持燭送歸院。

translations.literal: He was once summoned for night audience; the emperor ordered an inner attendant to hold a candle and escort him back to the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was summoned for a night audience, and the emperor ordered an inner attendant to escort him back to the Hanlin Academy with a candle.

sentences.zh: 方盛暑，為蠲宿直，令三五日一至院；

translations.literal: It was high summer; to exempt him from overnight duty he was ordered to come to the academy once every three or five days;
translations.idiomatic: In the height of summer he was excused from overnight duty at the academy and told to report only every three to five days;

sentences.zh: 迥辭以非故事，乃聽俟秋還直。

translations.literal: Jiong declined on the grounds it was not precedent, and was then permitted to resume duty when autumn came.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong declined on the grounds that this was without precedent, and was permitted to resume regular duty when autumn came.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部侍郎，請分司西京，特拜工部尚書、集賢院學士、判西京留司御史臺。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Minister of War, he requested duty at the Western Capital branch office and was specially appointed Minister of Works, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and judge of the Western Capital branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Minister of War, he requested a post at the Western Capital. He was specially appointed Minister of Works, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and judge of the Western Capital branch of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 賜一子官河南，以就養。

translations.literal: One son was granted an office in Henan so he could support his parents nearby.
translations.idiomatic: One of his sons was granted an office in Henan so that Jiong could be near his parents in their old age.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Renzong acceded he was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong acceded to the throne, Jiong was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 居臺六年，累章請老，以太子少保致仕，給全俸，歲時賜賚如學士。

translations.literal: After six years at the Censorate he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement, retired as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with full salary, and received seasonal gifts like an academician.
translations.idiomatic: After six years at the Censorate he repeatedly memorialized for retirement and was granted leave as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with full salary and seasonal gifts equal to those of a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，迥年八十一，召宴太清樓，免舞蹈。

translations.literal: During the Tiansheng era, Jiong at eighty-one was summoned to a banquet at the Taiqing Tower and exempted from the dance of obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng reign, when Jiong was eighty-one, he was summoned to a banquet at the Taiqing Tower and excused from the ceremonial dance of obeisance.

sentences.zh: 子宗愨為知制誥，侍從同預宴。

translations.literal: His son Zongque was Drafting Drafter and attended the banquet together as a companion.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongque, then serving as Drafting Drafter, attended the banquet with him as a court companion.

sentences.zh: 迥坐御史中丞之南，與宰臣同賜御飛白大字。

translations.literal: Jiong was seated south of the Censor-in-Chief and together with the chief ministers was granted imperial flying-white large characters.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was seated south of the Censor-in-Chief and, together with the chief ministers, was granted large characters in the emperor's flying-white calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 既罷，所以寵賚者甚厚，進太子少傅。

translations.literal: When it ended the favors bestowed were very generous, and he was advanced to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet ended the gifts bestowed upon him were exceptionally generous, and he was advanced to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 後復召對延和殿，帝訪以《洪範》雨暘之應。

translations.literal: Later he was again summoned to audience in the Yanhe Hall; the emperor inquired of him regarding the Hong Fan's correspondence of rain and drought.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again summoned to audience in the Yanhe Hall, where the emperor asked him about the correspondences of rain and drought described in the Hong Fan.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「比年變災薦臻，此天所以警陛下。

translations.literal: He replied: "In recent years disasters and anomalies have come in succession—this is how Heaven warns Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In recent years disasters and anomalies have followed one upon another. This is Heaven's way of warning Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 願陛下修飭王事，以當天心，庶幾轉亂而為祥也。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would rectify and put in order the kingly affairs to accord with Heaven's heart—then perhaps disorder may be turned to auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will put the affairs of state in order to accord with Heaven's will, so that disorder may yet be turned into blessing.

sentences.zh: 」既而獻《斧扆》、《慎刑箴》，《大順》、《審刑》、《無盡燈頌》，凡五篇。

translations.literal: " He then presented the "Axe and Screen," the "Admonition on Careful Punishment," the "Great Accord," "Examination of Punishment," and the "Ode to the Endless Lamp"—five pieces in all.
translations.idiomatic: " He then presented five works: the "Axe and Screen," the "Admonition on Careful Punishment," the "Great Accord," "Examination of Punishment," and the "Ode to the Endless Lamp."

sentences.zh: 及感疾，絕人事，屏醫藥，具冠服而卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: When he fell ill he cut off human affairs, set aside medicine, donned cap and robes, and died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When illness came upon him he withdrew from worldly affairs, refused medicine, donned his official cap and robes, and died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 罷朝一日，贈太子太保，諡文元。

translations.literal: Court was suspended one day; he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning was observed for one day. He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 迥善吐納養生之術，通釋、老書，以經傳傅致，為一家之說。

translations.literal: Jiong was skilled in breathing and nurturing life techniques, mastered Buddhist and Daoist books, and by applying the classics and commentaries formed a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was skilled in breathing exercises and the arts of nurturing life, mastered Buddhist and Daoist writings, and developed a distinctive doctrine by applying the classics and their commentaries.

sentences.zh: 性樂易寬簡，服道履正，雖貴勢無所屈，歷官臨事，未嘗挾情害物。

translations.literal: By nature he was cheerful, easy, broad, and simple; he followed the Way and trod the upright path—though noble power did not bend him, and in successive offices facing affairs he never harbored private feeling to harm others.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was cheerful, easygoing, and magnanimous. He followed the Way and held to what was right, never bending before power or rank, and in all his offices he never allowed private feeling to harm others.

sentences.zh: 真宗數稱其好學長者。

translations.literal: Zhenzong repeatedly praised him as a lover of learning and an elder worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong repeatedly praised him as a devoted scholar and venerable elder.

sentences.zh: 楊億嘗謂迥所作書命無過褒，得代言之體。

translations.literal: Yang Yi once said that Jiong's drafted commands never exceeded praise and attained the style of one who speaks for another.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi once remarked that Jiong's drafted edicts never exceeded due praise and always captured the proper style of imperial utterance.

sentences.zh: 喜質正經史疑義，摽括字類。

translations.literal: He delighted in questioning doubtful points in the classics and histories and in compiling categories of characters.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in resolving doubtful points in the classics and histories and in compiling classified lists of characters.

sentences.zh: 有以術命語迥，迥曰：「自然之分，天命也。

translations.literal: Someone spoke to Jiong of fate by arts of destiny; Jiong said: "The portion that is natural is Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When someone spoke to him of fate through divination, Jiong said, "What is natural in one's lot is Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 樂天不憂，知命也。

translations.literal: To rejoice in Heaven and not worry is knowing one's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: To rejoice in Heaven and not worry is to know one's mandate.

sentences.zh: 推理安常，委命也。

translations.literal: To reason from principle and rest in the constant is entrusting oneself to mandate.
translations.idiomatic: To reason from principle and rest in what is constant is to entrust oneself to mandate.

sentences.zh: 何必逆計未然乎？

translations.literal: Why must one plot in advance against what has not yet come?
translations.idiomatic: Why plot in advance against what has not yet come to pass?

sentences.zh: 」所著《翰林集》三十卷，《道院集》十五卷，《法藏碎金錄》十卷，《耆智餘書》、《隨因紀述》、《昭德新編》各三卷。

translations.literal: " His works included the Hanlin Collection in thirty juan, the Daoist Abbey Collection in fifteen juan, the Record of Fragmented Gold from the Dharma Storehouse in ten juan, and the Remaining Writings of Elder Wisdom, Records Following Causes, and the New Compilation of Manifest Virtue, each in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: " His writings included the Hanlin Collection in thirty juan, the Daoist Abbey Collection in fifteen juan, the Record of Fragmented Gold from the Dharma Storehouse in ten juan, and the Remaining Writings of Elder Wisdom, Records Following Causes, and the New Compilation of Manifest Virtue, each in three juan.

sentences.zh: 子宗愨。

translations.literal: Son Zongque.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongque.

sentences.zh: 子 宗愨

translations.literal: Son Zongque
translations.idiomatic: Son Zongque

sentences.zh: 元昊反，關中久宿師，以宗愨安撫陝西，與夏竦議攻守策。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, troops had long been stationed in Guanzhong; Zongque was sent to pacify Shaanxi and with Xia Song discussed offensive and defensive strategies.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled and troops had long been stationed in Guanzhong, Zongque was sent to pacify Shaanxi and discussed offensive and defensive strategies with Xia Song.

sentences.zh: 未還，道拜右諫議大夫、參知政事。

translations.literal: Before he returned, on the road he was appointed Right Remonstrating Grand Master and Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could return, he was appointed on the road Right Remonstrating Grand Master and Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷以金飾胡床及金汲器賜唃廝羅，宗愨曰：「仲叔於奚辭邑請繁纓，孔子曰：『不如多與之邑。

translations.literal: When the court was about to grant Gusaluo a gold-inlaid barbarian couch and gold water-drawing vessels, Zongque said: "Zhongshu at Xi declined the fief and requested the grand tassel; Confucius said: 'Better to give him more fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: When the court prepared to grant Gusaluo a gold-inlaid barbarian couch and gold water vessels, Zongque said, "When Zhongshu of the state of Xi declined a fief and asked instead for the grand tassel, Confucius said, 'Better to give him more fiefs.

sentences.zh: 』繁纓，諸侯之馬飾，猶不可與陪臣，況以乘輿之器賜外臣乎？

translations.literal: ' The grand tassel was a feudal lord's horse ornament—yet it could not be given to a ministerial retainer; how much less can vessels of the imperial carriage be granted to an outer minister?
translations.idiomatic: ' The grand tassel was an ornament for a feudal lord's horse—yet it could not be given to a ministerial retainer. How much less should vessels of the imperial carriage be granted to a foreign subject?

sentences.zh: 必欲優其禮，不若加賜金帛。

translations.literal: If one must honor his ritual, better to add gifts of gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: If the court wishes to honor him, it would be better to add gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 」後從帝郊祠感疾，數求罷，除資政殿學士、給事中。

translations.literal: " Later, following the emperor in suburban sacrifice he fell ill, repeatedly begged to resign, and was appointed Academician of the Hall of Sagacious Governance and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, while accompanying the emperor on a suburban sacrifice he fell ill and repeatedly asked to resign. He was appointed Academician of the Hall of Sagacious Governance and Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 數日，卒。

translations.literal: Within several days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days he died.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書，諡文莊。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 宗愨性敦厚，事父母孝，篤於故舊，凡任子恩皆先其族人。

translations.literal: Zongque's nature was sincere and thick; he served his parents filially, was devoted to old friends, and whenever yin privilege for office arose he always placed his clansmen first.
translations.idiomatic: Zongque was sincere and generous by nature. He served his parents filially, was devoted to old friends, and whenever yin privilege for office arose he always placed his clansmen first.

sentences.zh: 在翰林，一夕草將相五制，褒揚訓戒，人得所宜。

translations.literal: In the Hanlin, in one night he drafted five edicts for chief ministers and generals—praise, promotion, and admonition—each person receiving what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: While in the Hanlin Academy he once drafted five edicts for chief ministers and generals in a single night—of praise, promotion, and admonition—each suited to its recipient.

sentences.zh: 嘗密詔訪邊策，陳七事，頗施用之。

translations.literal: He was once secretly edicted to inquire into frontier strategy; he set forth seven matters, many of which were put into use.
translations.idiomatic: He was once secretly instructed to advise on frontier strategy and set forth seven proposals, many of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 劉筠，字子儀，大名人。

translations.literal: Liu Yun, style name Ziyi, was a man of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun, styled Ziyi, was a native of Daming.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為館陶縣尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became sheriff of Guantao County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed sheriff of Guantao County.

sentences.zh: 還，會詔知制誥楊億試選人校太清樓書，擢筠第一，以大理評事為秘閣校理。

translations.literal: On return, it happened that an edict ordered Drafting Drafter Yang Yi to test candidates in collating books at the Taiqing Tower; Yun was selected first and made Collator of the Imperial Library as Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, an edict ordered Yang Yi, then Drafting Drafter, to examine candidates for collating books at the Taiqing Tower. Yun ranked first and was appointed Collator of the Imperial Library with the rank of Assessor in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 真宗北巡，命知大名府觀察判官事。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong toured the north he was ordered to serve as administrative judge for the Daming observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong toured the north, Yun was appointed administrative judge on the staff of the Daming observation commission.

sentences.zh: 自邊鄙罷兵，國家閑暇，帝垂意篇籍，始集諸儒考論文章，為一代之典。

translations.literal: Since the borderlands ceased warfare the state had leisure; the emperor turned his mind to books and records and first gathered the Confucians to examine and discuss literature, making a canon for the age.
translations.idiomatic: After warfare on the frontier ceased and the empire entered a period of peace, the emperor turned his attention to literature and gathered Confucian scholars to examine and discuss texts, producing a literary canon for the age.

sentences.zh: 筠預修圖經及《冊府元龜》，推為精敏。

translations.literal: Yun participated in compiling the geographical treatise and the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives and was praised as keen and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Yun took part in compiling the geographical treatise and the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives and was regarded as exceptionally sharp and capable.

sentences.zh: 真宗將祀汾睢，屢得嘉雪，召筠及監察御史陳從易崇和殿賦歌詩，帝數稱善。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong was about to sacrifice at Fen-sui, auspicious snow fell repeatedly; he summoned Yun and Investigating Censor Chen Congyi to the Chonghe Hall to compose songs and poems, and the emperor repeatedly praised them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong was preparing to sacrifice at Fen-sui, auspicious snow fell repeatedly. He summoned Yun and Investigating Censor Chen Congyi to the Chonghe Hall to compose songs and poems, and repeatedly praised their work.

sentences.zh: 車駕西巡，又命筠纂土訓。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured the west, he again ordered Yun to compile the local customs records.
translations.idiomatic: During the imperial tour of the west, the emperor again ordered Yun to compile records of local customs.

sentences.zh: 是時四方獻符瑞，天子方興禮文之事，筠數上賦頌。

translations.literal: At that time the four quarters presented omens and auspicious signs; the Son of Heaven was just then promoting ritual and literary affairs, and Yun repeatedly submitted fu and eulogies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the regions submitted omens and auspicious signs, and the emperor was promoting ritual and literary projects. Yun repeatedly submitted rhapsodies and eulogies.

sentences.zh: 及《冊府元龜》成，進左正言、直史館、修起居注。

translations.literal: When the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives was completed he was advanced to Left Remonstrator, duty officer of the History Office, and compiler of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives was completed, he was promoted to Left Remonstrator, duty officer of the History Office, and compiler of the Imperial Diary.

sentences.zh: 嘗屬疾，予告滿，輒再予，積二百日，每詔續其奉。

translations.literal: He once fell ill; when sick leave was exhausted it was granted again, accumulating two hundred days, and each time an edict continued his salary.
translations.idiomatic: He once fell seriously ill. When his sick leave expired it was renewed, until he had accumulated two hundred days of leave, and the court repeatedly issued edicts continuing his salary.

sentences.zh: 遷左司諫、知制誥，加史館修撰，出知鄧州，徙陳州。
