translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Censorate Remonstrator and Drafting Drafter, given additional post as History Office compiler, sent out as prefect of Dengzhou, and transferred to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Censorate Remonstrator and Drafting Drafter, additionally appointed History Office compiler, then sent out as prefect of Dengzhou and transferred to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，糾察在京刑獄，知貢舉，遷尚書兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: On return he inspected capital judicial prisons, directed the examinations, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he inspected judicial prisons in the capital, directed the civil service examinations, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 復請鄧州，未行，進翰林學士。

translations.literal: He again requested Dengzhou; before he departed he was advanced to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He again requested an appointment at Dengzhou, but before he could depart he was promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 初，筠嘗草丁謂與李迪罷相制，既而謂復留，令別草制，筠不奉詔，乃更召晏殊。

translations.literal: Earlier Yun had once drafted the edict removing Ding Wei and Li Di from the chief ministership; afterward Wei was retained and he was ordered to draft another edict—Yun did not obey the edict, and Yan Shu was summoned instead.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yun had drafted the edict removing Ding Wei and Li Di from office. When Wei was later retained, the court ordered a new edict drafted. Yun refused to obey, and Yan Shu was summoned in his place.

sentences.zh: 筠自院出，遇殊樞密院南門，殊側面而過，不敢揖，蓋內有所愧也。

translations.literal: Yun left the academy and met Shu at the south gate of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Shu passed sideways and dared not bow—presumably feeling guilt within.
translations.idiomatic: As Yun left the Hanlin Academy he met Yan Shu at the south gate of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Shu passed by sideways without daring to bow, evidently ashamed within.

sentences.zh: 帝久疾，謂浸擅權，筠曰：「奸人用事，安可一日居此。

translations.literal: The emperor was long ill and Wei gradually usurped power; Yun said: "Wicked men hold affairs—how can one remain here a single day?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was long ill and Ding Wei gradually usurped power. Yun said, "With wicked men in control, how can one remain here even a single day?

sentences.zh: 」請補外，以右諫議大夫知廬州。

translations.literal: " He requested an outside appointment and was made Right Remonstrating Grand Master and prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He requested an outside appointment and was appointed Right Remonstrating Grand Master and prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷給事中，復召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Renzong acceded he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and again summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong acceded to the throne, Yun was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and again summoned as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 逾月，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 先是，三院御史言事，皆先白中丞。

translations.literal: Previously, when censors of the three bureaus spoke on affairs they all first informed the chief censor.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when censors of the three bureaus submitted memorials they always informed the chief censor first.

sentences.zh: 筠榜臺中：「御史自言事，毋白丞雜知」。

translations.literal: Yun posted in the bureau: "Censors speaking on their own affairs need not inform the chief or the miscellaneous supervisors."
translations.idiomatic: Yun posted a notice in the Censorate: "Censors presenting memorials on their own initiative need not inform the chief censor or the miscellaneous supervisors."

sentences.zh: 天聖二年貢舉，數以疾告，進尚書禮部侍郎、樞密直學士、知潁州。

translations.literal: At the Tiansheng second-year examinations he repeatedly reported illness, was advanced to Vice Minister of Rites in the Secretariat, Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the civil service examinations of the second year of Tiansheng he repeatedly reported illness. He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 召還，復知貢舉，進翰林學士承旨兼龍圖閣直學士、同修國史、判尚書都省。

translations.literal: Recalled, he again directed the examinations and was advanced to Hanlin Academician Expositor with concurrent Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, joint compiler of the National History, and judge of the Secretariat's general office.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he again directed the examinations and was promoted to Hanlin Academician Expositor with concurrent Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, joint compiler of the National History, and judge of the Secretariat's general office.

sentences.zh: 祀南郊，為禮儀使，請宿齋太廟日，罷朝饗玉清昭應宮，俟禮成，備鑾駕恭謝。

translations.literal: At the southern suburb sacrifice he was ritual commissioner and requested that on the day of fasting at the Imperial Ancestral Temple the court breakfast at the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace be suspended, and after the rite was completed the imperial carriage be prepared for reverent thanksgiving.
translations.idiomatic: At the southern suburb sacrifice he served as ritual commissioner and requested that on the day of fasting at the Imperial Ancestral Temple the court breakfast at the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace be suspended, and that after the rite was completed the imperial carriage be prepared for a formal thanksgiving ceremony.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his request.

sentences.zh: 筠素愛廬江，遂築室城中，構閣藏前後所賜書，帝飛白書曰「真宗聖文秘奉之閣」。

translations.literal: Yun had always loved Lujiang and therefore built a house in the city, constructing a pavilion to store books granted before and after; the emperor wrote in flying white: "Pavilion for Reverent Keeping of Zhenzong's Sagely Texts."
translations.idiomatic: Yun had always loved Lujiang and built a house in the city, constructing a pavilion to store books the emperor had granted him over the years. The emperor wrote its name in flying-white calligraphy: "Pavilion for Reverent Keeping of Zhenzong's Sagely Texts."

sentences.zh: 再知廬州，營塚墓，作棺，自為銘刻之。

translations.literal: Again administering Luzhou, he arranged tomb and grave, made a coffin, and carved his own epitaph on it.
translations.idiomatic: When he again served as prefect of Luzhou, he prepared his tomb and grave, made his own coffin, and carved his epitaph upon it.

sentences.zh: 既病，徙於書閣，卒。

translations.literal: When he fell ill he moved to the book pavilion and died.
translations.idiomatic: When illness came upon him he moved into his book pavilion and died there.

sentences.zh: 筠，景德以來，居文翰之選，其文辭善對偶，尤工為詩。

translations.literal: Yun, from the Jingde era onward, stood among literary selections; his prose excelled in parallelism and he was especially skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jingde reign onward Yun stood at the forefront of literary talent. His prose excelled in parallel construction, and he was especially accomplished as a poet.

sentences.zh: 初為楊億所識拔，後遂與齊名，時號「楊劉」。

translations.literal: At first he was recognized and promoted by Yang Yi; later he came to share equal fame, and the age called them "Yang and Liu."
translations.idiomatic: He was first recognized and promoted by Yang Yi, and later came to share equal fame with him. Contemporaries called them "Yang and Liu."

sentences.zh: 凡三入禁林，又三典貢部，以策論升降天下士，自筠始。

translations.literal: In all he entered the forbidden grove three times and directed the examination bureau three times; using policy essays to raise and lower scholars under Heaven began with Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy three times and directed the examination bureau three times. The practice of ranking candidates nationwide by policy essays began with him.

sentences.zh: 性不苟合，遇事明達，而其治尚簡嚴。

translations.literal: By nature he did not compromise lightly; in affairs he was clear-sighted, and in governance he valued simplicity and severity.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he did not compromise easily. In public affairs he was clear-sighted, and in governance he favored simplicity and strictness.

sentences.zh: 然晚為陽翟同姓富人奏求恩澤，清議少之。

translations.literal: Yet in his later years he memorialized on behalf of a wealthy man of the same surname at Yangdi seeking favors, and pure critics looked down on this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his later years he memorialized on behalf of a wealthy clansman at Yangdi seeking imperial favors, and upright opinion held this against him.

sentences.zh: 著《冊府應言》、《榮遇》、《禁林》、《肥川》、《中司》、《汝陰》、《三入玉堂》凡七集。

translations.literal: He authored seven collected works: Responses from the Imperial Archives, Honored Encounters, Forbidden Grove, Feichuan, Central Bureau, Ruyin, and Three Entries to the Jade Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He authored seven collected works: Responses from the Imperial Archives, Honored Encounters, Forbidden Grove, Feichuan, Central Bureau, Ruyin, and Three Entries to the Jade Hall.

sentences.zh: 一子蚤卒，田廬沒官。

translations.literal: One son died young; fields and houses were confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: His only son died young, and his fields and houses were confiscated by the state.

sentences.zh: 包拯少時，頗為筠所知。

translations.literal: When Bao Zheng was young he was rather well known to Yun.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao Zheng was young, Yun took considerable notice of him.

sentences.zh: 及拯顯，奏其族子為後，又請還所沒田廬云。

translations.literal: When Zheng rose to prominence he memorialized that a clansman's son be made heir and also requested return of the confiscated fields and houses.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao rose to prominence he memorialized that a clansman's son be made Yi's heir and also requested the return of the confiscated property.

sentences.zh: 薛映，字景陽，唐中書令元超八世孫，後家於蜀。

translations.literal: Xue Ying, style name Jingyang, was eighth-generation descendant of Tang Secretariat Director Yuan Chao; later the family settled in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying, styled Jingyang, was an eighth-generation descendant of Tang Secretariat Director Xue Yuan Chao. His family later settled in Shu.

sentences.zh: 父允中，事孟氏為給事中。

translations.literal: His father Yunzhong served the Meng house as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yunzhong served the Meng regime as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，為尚書都官郎中。

translations.literal: On submitting to the Song he became Director of the General Office in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting to the Song dynasty he became Director of the General Office in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 映進士及第，授大理評事，歷通判綿、宋、昇州，累遷太常丞。

translations.literal: Ying passed the jinshi examination with honors, was appointed Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, successively served as vice-prefect of Mian, Song, and Sheng prefectures, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Ying passed the jinshi examination with honors and was appointed Assessor in the Court of Judicial Review. He served successively as vice-prefect of Mian, Song, and Sheng prefectures and rose through successive promotions to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 王化基薦為監察御史、知開封縣。

translations.literal: Wang Huaji recommended him as Investigating Censor and magistrate of Kaifeng County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huaji recommended him as Investigating Censor and magistrate of Kaifeng County.

sentences.zh: 太宗召對，為江南轉運使，改左正言、直昭文館，為江、淮、兩浙茶鹽制置副使。

translations.literal: Taizong summoned him for audience; he became Jiangnan transport commissioner, was changed to Left Remonstrator and duty officer of the Zhaowen Hall, and was made Deputy Commissioner for Tea and Salt in Jiang, Huai, and the two Zhe regions.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned him for audience and appointed him Jiangnan transport commissioner. He was then promoted to Left Remonstrator and duty officer of the Zhaowen Hall and appointed Deputy Commissioner for Tea and Salt in the Jiang, Huai, and two Zhe regions.

sentences.zh: 改京東轉運使，徙河東，兼河西隨軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to Jingdong transport commissioner, transferred to Hedong, and concurrently followed the army in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jingdong transport commissioner, then to Hedong, with concurrent duty following the army in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 求便親，知相州。

translations.literal: He requested convenience for his kin and became prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a post convenient to his family and was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 再領漕京東，積遷尚書禮部郎中，擢知制誥，權判吏部流內銓兼制置群牧使。

translations.literal: He again headed Jingdong transport, was gradually promoted to Director of the Ministry of Rites in the Secretariat, was elevated to Drafting Drafter, and acted as judge of the Ministry of Personnel's internal selection with concurrent duty as Commissioner of Herds.
translations.idiomatic: He again headed transport in Jingdong, rose through successive promotions to Director of the Ministry of Rites, was elevated to Drafting Drafter, and served as acting judge of the Ministry of Personnel's internal selection with concurrent duty as Commissioner of Herds.

sentences.zh: 同梁顥安撫河北，還，權判度支。

translations.literal: Together with Liang Hao he pacified Hebei; on return he acted as judge of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Liang Hao he served as pacification commissioner in Hebei. On his return he acted as judge of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 映以右諫議大夫知杭州。

translations.literal: Ying was made Right Remonstrating Grand Master and prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was appointed Right Remonstrating Grand Master and prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 映臨決蜂銳，庭無留事。

translations.literal: Ying decided cases with sharp swiftness like a hornet; nothing remained in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Ying decided cases with swift and piercing judgment, leaving no backlog in his court.

sentences.zh: 轉運使姚鉉移屬州：「當直司毋得輒斷徒以上罪。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Yao Xian sent to subordinate prefectures: "The duty office must not on its own decide crimes above penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Yao Xian sent instructions to subordinate prefectures: "The duty office must not on its own decide cases involving penal servitude or heavier punishments.

sentences.zh: 」映即奏：「徒、流、笞、杖，自有科條，苟情狀明白，何必繫獄，以累和氣。

translations.literal: " Ying at once memorialized: "Penal servitude, exile, beating with the rod, and cudgeling each have their statutes—if the circumstances are clear, why must one imprison and thereby harm harmonious qi?
translations.idiomatic: " Ying immediately memorialized: "Penal servitude, exile, beating with the rod, and cudgeling each have their statutory provisions. If the circumstances are clear, why must offenders be imprisoned and thereby harm public harmony?

sentences.zh: 請詔天下，凡徒流罪於長吏前對辨，無所異，聽遣決之。

translations.literal: I request an edict to the empire that for all penal servitude and exile crimes, if argued before the chief official without objection, they be permitted to be decided and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: I request an edict to the empire that for all cases of penal servitude and exile, if the facts are argued before the chief official without dispute, the offender be permitted to be sentenced and released immediately.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷施用其言。

translations.literal: " The court applied his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The court adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 與鉉既不協，遂發鉉納部內女口及鬻銅器抑取其直，又廣市綾羅不輸稅。

translations.literal: Since he and Xian were not in accord, he then exposed that Xian had taken women and children within his jurisdiction and sold bronze vessels while suppressing their price, and also widely purchased silk gauze without paying tax.
translations.idiomatic: Because he and Yao Xian were at odds, he exposed that Xian had seized women and children within his jurisdiction, sold bronze vessels while suppressing their prices, and purchased silk gauze on a large scale without paying tax.

sentences.zh: 真宗遣御史臺推勘官儲拱劾鉉，得實，貶連州文學。

translations.literal: Zhenzong sent Censorate investigating officer Chu Gong to impeach Xian; the facts were established and Xian was demoted to Literary Officer of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong sent Censorate investigating officer Chu Gong to impeach Yao Xian. The charges were substantiated and Xian was demoted to Literary Officer at Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 映坐嘗召人取告鉉狀，當贖金，帝特貰之。

translations.literal: Ying was implicated because he had once summoned someone to obtain a report on Xian's conduct and should have paid redemption gold; the emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was implicated because he had once summoned someone to obtain evidence against Xian and was liable for a fine in redemption gold, but the emperor specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 在杭五年，入知通進銀臺司兼門下封駁事。

translations.literal: After five years at Hangzhou he entered to direct the Office for Presenting Memorials and the Silver Terrace with concurrent seal-and-return matters at the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: After five years at Hangzhou he was recalled to direct the Office for Presenting Memorials and the Silver Terrace while concurrently handling seal-and-return review at the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，為東京留守判官，遷給事中、勾當三班院，出知河南府。

translations.literal: At the Mount Tai feng he was staff judge for the Eastern Capital garrison, was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and administrator of the Three-Rank Bureau, and went out as prefect of Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the Mount Tai feng he served as staff judge for the Eastern Capital garrison, was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and administrator of the Three-Rank Bureau, and was appointed prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰還，駐蹕西京，以映有治狀，賜御書嘉獎。

translations.literal: Returning from the Fen-yin sacrifice, the court halted at the Western Capital; because Ying had achievements in governance, he was granted imperial writing in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the Fen-yin sacrifice, the court halted at the Western Capital. Because of Ying's record of effective governance, the emperor granted him an inscription of commendation in the imperial hand.

sentences.zh: 映好學有文，該覽強記，善筆劄，章奏尺牘，下筆立成。

translations.literal: Ying loved learning and possessed literary skill, read comprehensively and remembered strongly, was skilled in letters—memorials and documents were finished as soon as he put brush to paper.
translations.idiomatic: Ying loved learning and was accomplished in letters. He read widely and remembered with exceptional strength, and was skilled at drafting memorials and documents, which he completed the moment he set brush to paper.

sentences.zh: 為治嚴明，吏不能欺。

translations.literal: In governance he was stern and clear; clerks could not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: In governance he was stern and clear-sighted, and his subordinates could not deceive him.

sentences.zh: 每五鼓冠帶，黎明據案決事，雖寒暑，無一日異也。

translations.literal: Every fifth drum-watch he donned cap and belt; at dawn he sat at the desk to decide affairs—through cold and heat, not a single day differed.
translations.idiomatic: Every day at the fifth watch he donned his cap and belt, and at dawn he sat at his desk to decide cases. Through heat and cold alike, he never varied this routine by a single day.

sentences.zh: 子耀卿，秘閣校理。

translations.literal: Son Yaoqing was Collator of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yaoqing served as Collator of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 孫紳，直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: Grandson Shen was duty academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shen served as duty academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自唐末詞氣浸敝，迄於五季甚矣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: From late Tang literary spirit gradually decayed, reaching its extreme by the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: From late Tang onward literary spirit gradually decayed, reaching its nadir in the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 先民有言：「政厖土裂，大音不完，必混一而後振。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "When government is chaotic and the land splits apart, the great sound is incomplete—only after unification can it revive.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "When government falls into disorder and the land splits apart, the great cultural voice cannot be whole—only after unification can it revive.

sentences.zh: 」宋一海內，文治日起。

translations.literal: " Song unified the realm within the four seas, and literary governance rose day by day.
translations.idiomatic: " Once the Song unified the realm, literary culture rose day by day.

sentences.zh: 楊億首以辭章擅天下，為時所宗，蓋其清忠鯁亮之氣，未卒大施，悉發於言，宜乎雄偉而浩博也。

translations.literal: Yang Yi was first to dominate the realm through literary composition and was revered by the age—presumably because his pure, loyal, and upright bright spirit, not fully deployed before death, was all released in words; no wonder his style was grand and vast.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi was the first to dominate the literary world through his compositions and was revered by his age. His pure, loyal, and upright spirit, never fully deployed in public life, found its full expression in words—no wonder his style was grand and expansive.

sentences.zh: 劉筠後出，能與齊名，氣象似爾，至於文體之今古，時習使然，遑暇議是哉。

translations.literal: Liu Yun came later and could share equal fame; his bearing was similar. As for whether literary style is ancient or modern, the habits of the age make it so—who has leisure to debate right and wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun came later and could share equal fame; his literary bearing was much the same. Whether style should be ancient or modern was simply a matter of the habits of the age—who had leisure to debate the point?

sentences.zh: 晁迥寬易，與物無忤，父子先後典書命，稱為名臣。

translations.literal: Chao Jiong was broad and easy, at odds with nothing; father and son in succession directed book commands and were called famous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Jiong was magnanimous and easygoing, at odds with no one. Father and son in succession directed imperial edicts and were acclaimed as eminent ministers.

sentences.zh: 薛映學藝、吏術俱優，而挾忿以抉人之私，君子病之。

translations.literal: Xue Ying was excellent in both scholarly arts and administrative technique, yet he harbored resentment to expose others' private faults—the gentleman finds this regrettable.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying excelled in both scholarship and administrative skill, yet he harbored resentment and used it to expose others' private failings—a fault that men of principle regretted.
